one_liner: Cloud-based messaging platform with two main developer surfaces: the HTTPS Bot API for bots/mini apps and the MTProto client API for full-featured clients; plus “Log in with Telegram” for user authentication.
access_notes: Anyone can create a bot and obtain a token via @BotFather; api_id/api_hash for MTProto are issued self-serve at my.telegram.org.
mcp_notes: Community MCP servers exist (often Telethon-based) that enable agents to read/send messages via MTProto or the Bot API; no official vendor MCP.
blocker_notes: None. Credentials are self-serve via @BotFather for the Bot API and my.telegram.org for MTProto; standard bot constraints (can’t initiate user chats, rate limits) exist but don’t block integration.

evidence.quote: To get started, message @BotFather on Telegram to register your bot and receive its authentication token.
Use this method to specify a URL and receive incoming updates via an outgoing webhook. Whenever there is an update for the bot, we will send an HTTPS POST request to the specified URL…
Log in to your Telegram core: https://my.telegram.org. … You will get … the api_id and api_hash parameters required for user authorization.
Verify Claims: Check that ‘iss’ is ‘https://oauth.telegram.org’, ‘aud’ matches your Bot ID, and the token has not expired (‘exp’).
For bulk notifications, bots are not able to broadcast more than about 30 messages per second, unless they enable paid broadcasts to increase the limit.
Developers communicate with this server via an easy HTTPS-interface … known as the Bot API.
MTProto bot auth also exists for advanced cases (e.g., auth.importBotAuthorization) via MTProto

_trail.quote: Access is self_serve_free, so changed buildability from ready_with_caveats to ready while keeping blocker as none to resolve the inconsistency.
